correctness.rationale: Exact endpoint values give the optimal upper bound. For each prime dividing the two consecutive integers k+1 and k+2, elementary binomial coefficient identities give the lower bound; the four-consecutive-integers residue analysis proves there is no deficiency for primes at least five, at most one two-adic factor already removed from B, and precisely the possible one three-adic factor. The zero-boundary conventions are included, and an independent program checks 100 finite prefixes and 20 complete Newton-coefficient gcds.

value.rationale: The fixed divisor is the sharp integer-valued normalization of a natural product of binomial-basis elements. Shifting by two is the first nonadjacent equal-lower-index product and has a nontrivial mod-three classification with a sharp denominator, not implied merely by the content of each factor. The theorem settles the full natural infinite family for this object and supplies the unexpected two-value certificate. No claim about all shifts or general polynomials is made.
